Across four models (1.5B--13B, three families), complete execution traces (77--82\%) barely improve over source code alone (${\sim}$73--76\%) while compact exception events achieve ${\geq}$99.33\%; bidirectional cross-dataset transfer (99.4--100\%) and marker-removal robustness (97.65\% vs.\ regex collapse to 28.49\%) confirm SFT learns genuine diagnostic patterns.

These findings suggest prioritizing diagnostic density over completeness in trace-based tool design; gradient masking ablations and broader generalization remain as future work.

The primary seed is 42; seeds 123 and 456 test \texttt{exception\_only} robustness (Appendix~\ref{sec:training_details}).

\subsection{Loss Ablation}

To probe the contribution of gradient dilution, we introduce \texttt{full\_trace\_label\_only}: identical full-trace input but loss computed only on the verdict token (trace positions masked).
TRL's SFTTrainer computes mean cross-entropy over label tokens, so label-only loss does not amplify the effective learning rate.
However, this ablation simultaneously changes three variables: (1)~which tokens receive gradient updates, (2)~the implicit regularization from predicting trace tokens, and (3)~the training signal distribution.
The resulting improvement over standard \texttt{full\_trace} provides an \emph{upper-bound estimate} of gradient dilution's contribution; the remaining gap to VOTA reflects diagnostic signal dilution at inference, but the decomposition is approximate (\S\ref{sec:density}).

\paragraph{Controlled gradient masking.}
To isolate gradient dilution, we mask 99.8\% of gradient updates during \texttt{exception\_only} training, matching the diagnostic token ratio of full traces while preserving compact input.
This yields 98.99\% ($-$0.84pp from \texttt{exception\_only}), limiting gradient dilution to ${\leq}$5\% of the 18.07pp gap (Table~\ref{tab:density}).
Content quality---diagnostic signal density at inference---accounts for the remaining ${\geq}$95\%.

\caption{Decomposition of the full-trace degradation (Qwen-7B). Gradient masking isolates gradient dilution to ${\leq}$5\%; content quality (signal density at inference) accounts for ${\geq}$95\%. Label-only loss provides a confounded but directionally consistent complementary estimate.}

\section{Conclusion}

Across four models (1.5B--13B, three families), complete execution traces (77--82\%) barely improve over source code alone (${\sim}$73--76\%) while compact exception events achieve ${\geq}$99.33\%; bidirectional cross-dataset transfer (99.4--100\%) and marker-removal robustness (97.65\% vs.\ regex collapse to 28.49\%) confirm SFT learns genuine diagnostic patterns.
A two-tier signal hierarchy yields a practical fallback (exceptions first, tail-truncated state otherwise); gradient masking limits gradient dilution to ${\leq}$5\%, confirming content quality as the dominant factor (${\geq}$95\%).
These findings suggest prioritizing diagnostic density over completeness; broader generalization remains as future work.
